headline: Proposed swimming pool at 11 Lojko Drive and public dog park on L Pine Street, plus redevelopment of 1 Pine Street Extension.
summary: Two projects would affect wetland buffers: a backyard pool on Lojko Drive and a public dog park on L Pine Street. The agenda also lists two 5-story multi-family buildings planned for 1 Pine Street Extension.
items: Public comment on pool proposal at 11 Lojko Drive, with 572 SF of permanent wetland buffer impact
Public comment on dog park proposal on L Pine Street, with 12,975 SF of permanent wetland buffer impact
Redevelopment of 1 Pine Street Extension (NIMCO) with two 5-story multi-family buildings, informational only
Discussion with SPNHF staff on possible ownership of parcel H-635 in the Northwest Sanctuary
Parcel I-10 (Narrows Road) in the Northwest Sanctuary retained by City for conservation
Differentiating conservation space vs. civic areas on the Nashua re-CODE draft zoning map for the Southwest Trails
Easement monitoring for the Northwest Sanctuary
Standardized fee-in-lieu monetary rate per inch DBH for non-replaceable trees
Bishop Guertin's day of service on November 5, 9:30am to 1:30pm
Committee reports on easement monitoring, digital marketing/website design, and land and trail management
Nonpublic session per RSA 91-A:3 (roll call vote required)
location: Room 208, Nashua City Hall, 229 Main Street, Nashua, NH
plain_text:
Next Regular Meeting: December 1, 2026 
 
 
City of Nashua 
Conservation Commission 
City Hall, 229 Main Street, PO Box 2019, Nashua NH 03061-2019 
(603) 589-3090         www.nashuanh.gov 
 
NASHUA CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
Notice is hereby given that a Public Meeting of the City of Nashua Conservation Commission will occur in Room 208 at the 
Nashua City Hall located at 229 Main Street, Nashua, NH on November 4, 2026 at 7pm. 
A. Call to Order 
B. Roll Call  
C. Approval of Minutes 
10/06/2026 NCC Regular Meeting 
 
D. Old Business - Public Comment Related to this Item (Limited to 3 Minutes per Speaker) 
 
None 
 
E. New Business - Public Comment Related to this Item (Limited to 3 Minutes per Speaker) 
 
Christine Sheridan, 11 Lojko Drive. Proposal to install a 20’ x 36’ inground, gunite swimming pool within the 
wetland buffer of a critical wetland, with permanent impact to 572 SF of the wetland buffer. Map B. Lot 2818. 
Zone R-18 B – Suburban Residence. Ward 9. 
 
City of Nashua, L Pine Street. Proposal to develop a public dog park, including 8 parking spaces, with 
permanent impact to 12,975 SF of the wetland buffer for a prime wetland. Map 77. Lot 5. Zone R-B – Urban 
Residence. Ward 4. 
 
F. NCC Correspondence and Communications 
 
1. City of Nashua, 1 Pine Street Extension (NIMCO). Proposal to redevelop this site by constructing 2 5-
story, multi-family residential buildings, including new roads, sidewalks, surface parking and understructure 
parking at both buildings. Map 77. Lot 30. Zone GI/MU – General Industrial/Mixed Use. Ward 4. Subject to 
Shoreland Exemption – Informational Only (No Vote). 
2. Discussion with SPNHF staff on the possible ownership of parcel H-635 in the Northwest Sanctuary. 
3. Parcel I-10 (Narrows Road) in the Northwest Sanctuary retained by City for conservation. 
4. Differentiating Conservation Space vs. Civic in the Nashua re-CODE draft zoning map, regarding the area 
of the Southwest Trails (Terrell Homestead, Buckmeadow, Lovewell Pond vs. Yudicky Park) 
 
G. Commissioners Discussion 
1. NHACC Membership Renewal. 
2. Approval of spending for trailblazing. 
3. Draft 2027 Meeting Dates. 
4. Easement monitoring for Northwest Sanctuary. 
5. Discuss establishing a standardized fee-in-lieu monetary rate per inch DBH for non-replaceable trees. 
6. Bishop Guertin’s day of service – November 5, 9:30am to 1:30pm. 
7. Other. 
 
H. Committee Reports 
1. Easement Monitoring. 
2. Digital Marketing/website design. 
3. Land and Trail Management. 
4. Other. 
 
I. Public Comment Related to Items on the Agenda (Limited to 3 Minutes per Speaker) 
J. Nonpublic Session per. RSA 91-A:3 (Roll call vote required). 
K. Adjournment 
 
Questions regarding the Agenda can be directed to Levent Akinci, Sustainability Planner, Sustainability 
Department (603) 589-3064.
